comment.comment: `//` to the end of the line. There are no block comments, so nothing here can span one.

string.comment: A string cannot span a line, so `end` is the closing quote OR the end of the line. Without the `$` an unterminated string colours the rest of the file, which is the usual fault in a grammar written from regular expressions.

patterns.comment: The seven escapes, and no others. `\u{...}` takes one to six hexadecimal digits: without the bound a stray `{` swallows the rest of the line.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.miru

patterns.comment: Anything else after a backslash is an error in the language, so it is marked rather than coloured as part of the text.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unknown-escape.miru

number.comment: A `_` sits between two digits only, so the pattern is a digit, then any number of groups of `_` and a digit. `1.` is the integer 1 and then a dot, so the fractional part needs a digit after the point. `_1` is an identifier, and the leading `\b` with no `_` in the first position keeps it that way.

keyword.comment: The 16 keywords, less the three that are values. Section 2.5 of the specification lists them.

literal.comment: `true`, `false`, and `nil` are values rather than control, and the playground colours them apart from the keywords for the same reason.

builtin.comment: The 53 builtins, longest first. Generated by scripts/build_grammar.sh from BUILTIN_NAMES in src/builtins.rs. Do not edit by hand.
